To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a 2D image representation is insufficient for understanding a scene; (2) a 3D representation that captures the viewpoint of an agent is crucial; (3) the role of the observer is an important factor in scene understanding; and (4) rich data is necessary for learning the right representation.

1) a scene-centric dataset is a better choice for 2D recognition; 2) a panoramic place representation is a good model of the human visual system, which can be learned from rich data; and 3) a place-centric 3D scene representation is a powerful tool to understand a scene, which can be obtained by modeling the computer as an agent in the scene.

• A scene-centric dataset provides more realistic benchmark for standard recognition tasks, which can be used to evaluate existing methods. • 3D geometric figures are a good representation for scene understanding, and can be learned from multiple viewpoint data.
